en: Meet Hopyard Designer, a shared planning workspace for hop farmers, installers, and their AI agents.
A hopyard plan connects planting density, poles, wire, anchors, wind load, and cost. One change affects the whole system.
The original web app already calculated seed cost, facility quantities, structural load, and live estimates from a human-operated design form.
Every input updates a construction-oriented two-dimensional plan, including poles, anchors, main wire, training wire, and hop positions.
The same design becomes an interactive three-dimensional farm. We can orbit the complete structure and inspect the system from any direction.
Zooming in reveals the reusable Blender assets: galvanized poles, perimeter anchors, wire hardware, and hops trained along the support lines. Then we zoom back out to the full farm.
For the WebMCP Challenge, we added five structured site tools instead of making an agent guess how to click the interface.
The agent first reads the active design, quantities, pricing status, safety status, regional profiles, and current collaboration state.
It then creates two non-destructive alternatives: a Korean I-shaped training layout and a sourced North American eighteen-foot Y-trained reference system.
spoken: It then creates two non-destructive alternatives: a Korean eye-shaped training layout and a sourced North American eighteen-foot Y-trained reference system.

en: Both candidates appear in the same visual workspace with differences in poles, wire, plant count, estimate, and engineering status.
The agent presents both options and waits. The farmer chooses the Korean I-shaped training alternative for visual preview.
spoken: The agent presents both options and waits. The farmer chooses the Korean eye-shaped training alternative for visual preview.

en: The selected candidate updates the shared two-dimensional and three-dimensional views while preserving an exact snapshot of the original design.
During preview, Apply and Discard are registered dynamically, increasing the tool count from five to seven. Final control remains with the farmer.
Here the farmer chooses Discard. The agent restores the previous design and returns to five tools, without inventing prices or engineering approval.
Hopyard Designer turns a complex agricultural estimate into a transparent human-agent design conversation, without taking final decisions away from the farmer.
Plan precisely, compare safely, and build with confidence. This is Hopyard Designer by HOPEDEN, powered by WebMCP.
